exposure: Maternal HIV viral load (detectable vs undetectable)
Mode of delivery (Caesarean section vs vaginal delivery)
cohort: 84 HIV-positive women who delivered in a tertiary centre from January 2008 to December 2015
finding: The study found a perinatal HIV transmission rate of zero, suggesting that high standards of care for HIV-positive women have been successful in preventing perinatal transmission.
mod_finding: Caesarean section rates were higher among women with detectable viral loads (93.1%) compared to those with undetectable viral loads (58.7%).
